Application Materials.content:
As part of your online application, you also need to submit the following supporting documents:
- A copy (or copies) of your official degree certificate(s) (if you have already completed your degree)
- A copy (or copies) of your official academic transcript(s), showing full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained
- Official English translations of the certificate(s) and transcript(s)
- One reference letter on headed paper
- Evidence of your English language ability (if your first language is not English)
- Any additional documents required for this programme (see Entry requirements for this programme)
- A copy of the photo page of your passport
You have **42 days** to submit your application once you begin the process. You may save and return to your application as many times as you wish to update information, complete sections or upload supporting documents such as your final transcript or your language test.
**Reference**: Please provide one reference. This should typically be an academic reference but in cases where this is not possible then a reference from a current employer may be accepted instead. Certain programmes, such as the MBA programme, may also accept an employer reference. If you already have a copy of a reference on letter headed paper then please upload this to your application. If you do not already have a reference to upload then please enter your referee’s name and contact details on the online application and we will contact your referee directly.
For **Employment and Experience**, additional details may be attached in your personal statement/proposal where appropriate.

Application Deadlines.content:
- **Teaching start:** September
- **Application deadlines:** International & EU applicants: **24 August 2026**; Home applicants: **24 August 2026**

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Standard entry requirement:** **2.1 Hons (or non-UK equivalent)** in **Economics, Finance, Computing Science or another subject with a quantitative focus**.
- **China-specific academic entry requirement:** Bachelor degree at **70%/75%/80%/85%/87%** depending on university attended, with reference to **Result Required 2.1** on the China University Grade Equivalences List, in **Economics, Finance, Computing Science or another subject with a quantitative focus**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
For applicants from non-English speaking countries, as defined by the [UK Government](https://www.gov.uk/student-visa/knowledge-of-english), the University sets a minimum English Language proficiency level.
- **IELTS Academic and Academic Online (not General Training): 6.5 overall with no subtest less than 6.0**. IELTS One Skill Retake Accepted. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **TOEFL (ibt, mybest or athome)**: Tests taken up to 20 January 2026: **90 Overall**, no subtest lower than Reading 20; Listening 19; Speaking 19; Writing 21. Tests taken from 21 January 2026: **92 Overall**, no subtest lower than Reading 22; Listening 20; Speaking 23; Writing 21. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test, this includes TOEFL mybest.
- **Pearsons PTE Academic: 65 overall** with no subtest less than Reading 60; Listening 60; Speaking 65; Writing 60. Online PTE not accepted for entry. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Cambridge Proficiency in English (CPE) and Cambridge Advanced English (CAE): 176 overall with no subtest less than 169**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Oxford English Test: 7 overall with no subtest less than 6**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **LanguageCert Academic/ Academic Online: 70 overall with no subtest less than 65**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Password Skills Plus: 6.5 overall with no subtest less than 6.0**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Trinity College Integrated Skills in English II:** Two subtests at **96 or higher**, and two subtests at **80 or higher**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Kaplan Test of English:** Any two subtests at **480 or higher**, and any two subtests at **450 or higher**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months of programme start date**. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **University of Glasgow Pre-sessional courses:** Tests are accepted for **2 years following date of successful completion**.
Alternatives to English Language qualification:
- Degree from majority-English speaking country (as defined by the UKVI including Canada if taught in English) - students must have studied for a minimum of their final year at Undergraduate level, or **9 months at Master's level**, and must have completed their degree in that majority-English speaking country within the last **6 years**.
- Undergraduate 2+2 and 3+1 degrees from majority-English speaking country (as defined by the UKVI including Canada if taught in English) - students must have completed their final year of study in that majority-English speaking country within the last **6 years**.
For international students, the Home Office has confirmed that the University can choose to use these tests to make its own assessment of English language ability for visa applications to degree level programmes. The University is also able to accept UKVI approved Secure English Language Tests (SELT) but does not require a specific UKVI SELT for degree level programmes, and still accepts any of the English tests listed for admission to this programme.
The University of Glasgow accepts evidence of the required language level from the English for Academic Study Unit Pre-sessional courses. Pre-sessional courses provide direct entry to the University programme for successful students (no need to take IELTS). More information: [Pre-sessional courses](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/mlc/eas/pre-sessionalcourses/). The University can also consider pre-sessional courses accredited by BALEAP approved institutions: Heriot Watt, Kingston Upon Thames, Middlesex University, Manchester University, Reading University, Edinburgh University, ST Andrews University, UCL, and Durham.
As part of the online application, applicants need to submit evidence of English language ability if their first language is not English. In the online application guidance, under **English Language Proficiency**, applicants should state the date of any English language test taken (or to be taken) and the award date (or expected award date if known).

Program Overview.content:
The Masters in Data Analytics for Economics & Finance is a multi-disciplinary programme that prepares you for data-driven careers in economics and finance. It combines insights from economics, finance, statistics, and computing science. With a focus on rigorous data methods, graduates gain essential skills to inform complex decision-making. Jointly delivered by the Adam Smith Business School and the School of Computing Science, the programme provides future-proof, in-demand expertise for today’s fast-changing industries.
- **Teaching start:** September
- **Location:** [Glasgow: Gilmorehill campus](https://www.gla.ac.uk/explore/campuses/gilmorehill/)
- **MSc:** 12 months full-time
The programme offers a distinctive and innovative multi-disciplinary approach to data analytics as applied to economics and finance, comprising core and elective courses from the Departments of Economics, Accounting & Finance, and Computing Science. It provides advanced training to develop data analytic skills for successful careers in business or industry and also provides a solid foundation for PhD study. Students have the opportunity to participate in summer project internships with prestigious partners and can gain recognition for extra-curricular activities through the Adam Smith Business School’s Graduate Award Scheme. The programme is ranked in the top 70 of the [QS World University Business Masters Ranking 2026](https://www.topuniversities.com/business-masters-rankings/business-analytics), and students can experience practical learning with real business challenges through competitive, merit-based [industry projects](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=industryprojects). Industry Projects are not guaranteed; applications are subject to availability and review processes, and unsuccessful candidates can opt for a research proposal for their dissertation. Students can also secure their own projects with approval from academic and/or professional services.
[Adam Smith Business School is **triple accredited**](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/business/aboutus/accreditationsandrankings/accreditations/).
The programme provides advanced training in time series analysis, panel data econometrics and Bayesian inference, based on internationally-recognised research, to equip students to apply their knowledge and skills to conduct state-of-the-art research and lead and deliver projects. Pre-sessional courses ensure that students from different backgrounds can catch up to the required level of pre-requisite knowledge. Students take four core courses and a selection of optional courses. Over the summer months, students complete a dissertation, either under the standard research pathway or as part of an internship with one of the programme’s industry partners.
The Data Analytics for Economics & Finance MSc is suitable for those who have developed a strong interest in obtaining data analytic skills combined with economic insights and aspire to follow a career in finance, banking, consulting, government and other major international institutions. The programme delivers a multi-disciplinary curriculum that prepares graduates for work in all fields of data-rigorous professions related to economics and finance, as well as marketing and business. It is also advantageous for direct admission to a PhD programme. [See our alumni success stories](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/ouralumnisuccessstories/).

Curriculum.content:
- **Teaching start:** September; [Glasgow: Gilmorehill campus](https://www.gla.ac.uk/explore/campuses/gilmorehill/); **MSc: 12 months full-time**.
- The programme comprises core and elective courses offered from the Departments of Economics, Accounting & Finance, and Computing Science. Pre-sessional courses ensure that students from different backgrounds can catch up to the required level of pre-requisite knowledge.
- You will take four core courses and a selection of optional courses. Over the summer months you will also complete a dissertation, either under the standard research pathway, or as part of an internship with one of the industry partners.
Pre-sessional courses:
- Computational Statistics and Data Analytics
- Econometrics and Statistics Review
Core courses:
- [Applied Time Series and Forecasting](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=ECON5119)
- [Bayesian Data Analysis](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=ECON5120)
- [Microeconometrics: Impact Evaluation and Causal Analysis](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=ECON5121)
- [Statistical Machine Learning](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=ECON5129)
Optional courses:
- [Applied Computational Finance](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=ECON5065)
- [Asset Pricing: Theory and Empirics](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=ECON5069)
- [CyberSecurity Fundamentals for MSc (M)](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=COMPSCI5063)
- [Data Science for Marketing Analytics](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=MGT5372)
- [Deep Learning for MSc (M)](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=COMPSCI5103)*
- [Financial Information Retrieval](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=ACCFIN5233)
- [Text as Data for MSc](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=COMPSCI5106)*
Research project:
- [Dissertation DAEF Industry Pathway](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=ECON5122P) or [Dissertation DAEF Research Pathway](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=course&code=ECON5123P)
*Students who choose either Deep Learning for MSc (M) or Text as Data for MSc must also select Programming & Systems Development, offered in semester one, as a pre-requisite.
Industry Projects are not guaranteed. All applications are subject to availability and review processes; candidates who are unsuccessful can opt for a research proposal for their dissertation. Students can also secure their own projects with approval from academic and/or professional services.

Multiple Applications.content:
- Parallel applications to multiple programmes will be dealt with as separate applications at all times.
- Applicants must make a new application for each programme they want to be considered for.
- For some programmes, an application fee of **£25** may be charged.
- Applicants may accept more than one conditional offer but can only accept one unconditional offer.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
It may be possible to defer your offer to the next available intake. Deferral requests will be considered individually and are not guaranteed.
Deferral requests for the 2027 intake are open. To be considered for a deferral, you must have accepted a conditional or unconditional offer for the 2027 intake and have paid any relevant deposits to secure your place on the course. The deadline for requesting a deferral to the 2027 intake is **30 September 2026**. If you do not meet these criteria, your request will declined.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- Applicant deposit refunds may be available where the **applicant does not meet conditions of offer**: “This may be academic or language test requirements.” Satisfactory evidence must be uploaded to the applicant self-service to prove the conditions have not been met; applicants who do not meet the language condition must show a reasonable attempt, by providing **at least two language tests** taken after the deposit was paid.
- For English-language conditions, the University of Glasgow accepts evidence of the required language level from English for Academic Study Unit **Pre-sessional courses**. The courses offer “direct entry to your University programme for successful students (no need to take IELTS)” and are intended to “bring your English up to entry level for University study.” More information: [Pre-sessional courses](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/mlc/eas/pre-sessionalcourses/).
